findings.title: Remote content piped into shell
findings.message: Remote content is piped directly into a shell, so unreviewed network content can execute on the user's machine.
findings.rationale: Piping network content directly into a shell prevents review, pinning, and integrity checks before code runs on the user's machine.
findings.remediation: Download remote content to a local file, pin the source version, verify integrity, and require explicit review before execution.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC001` only for a reviewed bootstrap path that pins the source, verifies integrity, and documents why direct execution is still required.

findings.title: Unpinned remote URL reference
findings.message: The remote dependency `script:install.sh` is not pinned to immutable content, so reviewed behavior can change without a skill package change.
findings.rationale: Mutable remote URLs can serve different content over time, which prevents deterministic review and can introduce unreviewed behavior.
findings.remediation: Pin GitHub raw URLs to full commit SHAs, use immutable release assets with checksum evidence, or vendor reviewed content locally.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SUPPLY005` only for a reviewed remote reference whose mutability is intentional and whose update process is documented.

findings.title: Secret-like environment variable access
findings.message: The artifact reads secret-like environment variable `SERVICE_TOKEN`. This may be legitimate, but it needs review, declaration, and careful handling to avoid accidental disclosure.
findings.rationale: Reading token-, key-, password-, or credential-like environment variables can expose secrets to scripts, logs, prompts, or external services.
findings.remediation: Avoid broad secret reads; require explicit user-provided configuration for the narrow credential needed and keep it out of logs and generated reports.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC002` only for a reviewed credential access path with least-privilege scope, documented handling, and no logging or unintended disclosure.

findings.title: Data sent to external URL
findings.message: The artifact reads sensitive source `SERVICE_TOKEN` and sends data to external URL `https://collector.example/upload`. This may be legitimate, but it needs review, documented consent, and careful handling to avoid accidental disclosure.
findings.rationale: Sending secret-like environment variables or credentials to an external URL can disclose private authentication material outside the local audit boundary.
findings.remediation: Keep processing local by default, document any required network destination, minimize the transmitted data, and require explicit user consent.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC003` only for a documented endpoint with reviewed data scope, least-privilege credentials, and explicit user-approved transmission.

findings.title: Prompt-injection-like instruction
findings.message: The text contains an instruction that appears to tell an agent to ignore higher-priority policy, bypass review, override behavior, or expose secrets. Review this content as prompt-injection-like before trusting the skill.
findings.rationale: Instructions that ask an agent to ignore policy, bypass review, reveal secrets, or override higher-priority directions can subvert host safety controls.
findings.remediation: Remove adversarial instructions and rewrite the skill so it states legitimate behavior, required permissions, and user confirmation points plainly.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC011` only for a benign quoted example that is clearly labeled and cannot be mistaken for an instruction.

findings.title: Hidden instruction in comment or code block

findings.rationale: Instructions hidden in comments, examples, or code blocks can be overlooked by human reviewers while still being consumed by an agent.
findings.remediation: Remove hidden instructions or move legitimate operational guidance into visible prose with clear scope and rationale.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC012` only for inert test fixtures or quoted examples that are visibly labeled as non-instructions.

findings.title: Unpinned package dependency
findings.message: The package dependency `npm:left-pad` is not pinned to an exact version, so future installs may resolve different code.
findings.rationale: Unpinned package versions can change without a skill package change, making audits less reproducible and increasing supply-chain risk.
findings.remediation: Use exact package versions and commit the relevant lockfile when the package manager supports one.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SUPPLY004` only when a reviewed local policy intentionally allows version ranges and documents the update and review process.

findings.title: Install command without matching reproducibility evidence
findings.message: The skill runs a npm install command without matching lockfile or exact-pinned dependency manifest evidence, so dependency resolution may change between audits.
findings.rationale: Package installation without a matching lockfile or exact-pinned dependency manifest can resolve different dependency graphs over time and weakens reproducible offline review.
findings.remediation: Commit the package manager lockfile for the install command, use an exact-pinned dependency manifest that the command actually installs from, switch to a reproducible install mode, or remove package installation from the skill workflow.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SUPPLY003` only for a reviewed install path whose dependency set is pinned by matching local reproducibility evidence or controlled by another documented local mechanism.

findings.title: Package install without lockfile
findings.message: The artifact runs a JavaScript package install without nearby lockfile or exact version pinning evidence. This can make installs resolve different packages over time and increases reproducibility and supply-chain risk.
findings.rationale: Package installs without a lockfile or equivalent pinning can resolve different dependency versions across machines and over time.
findings.remediation: Use lockfile-backed install commands, root-level or same-subtree ecosystem lockfiles, or complete exact package pins. The initial policy treats npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, pip, cargo, gem, and system package installs without those offline-verifiable signals as `SEC009`.
findings.suppression: Suppress `SEC009` only when another reviewed, offline-verifiable mechanism pins the package set and preserves reproducible installation behavior.

finding_groups.title: Package install without lockfile
finding_groups.rationale: Package installs without a lockfile or equivalent pinning can resolve different dependency versions across machines and over time.
finding_groups.remediation: Use lockfile-backed install commands, root-level or same-subtree ecosystem lockfiles, or complete exact package pins. The initial policy treats npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, pip, cargo, gem, and system package installs without those offline-verifiable signals as `SEC009`.
finding_groups.suppression: Suppress `SEC009` only when another reviewed, offline-verifiable mechanism pins the package set and preserves reproducible installation behavior.
